prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1416; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer narrative: On arrival in Sugar Land, Texas, I found a rear-end collision involving two vehicles. Driver 1 was stopped in the travel lane when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear of the stopped car. Driver 1 reported pain in the lower back and said the impact pushed them forward against the seatbelt before rebounding into the seat. The severity of the impact appears consistent with that account. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. A Passenger was also present in the front seat, and both the statements of the drivers and the other occupant confirm that Driver 1 was inside the car at the time of impact. Damage to the rear bumper and trunk of Driver 1's vehicle matches the direction and force described by both drivers. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general layout and damage, though no independent witnesses came forward. Some older faint scratches were noted on the rear panel, which may predate this collision and will need to be reviewed separately. Driver 2 was cooperative and provided insurance information at the scene.
